title: Add a new motor skill using only a code on a frozen shared basis
hypothesis: A few-shot new skill lying in a frozen shared rank-2 action residual basis can be added by a compact Mirror code, preserving heldout action accuracy with lower total bytes and adaptation work than a fresh native rank-2 LoRA adapter.

world.new_skill: one heldout skill generated as a combination of frozen residual atoms

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed after exact native coefficient alias or failure of quality/bytes gate.

controls: Mirror coefficient code on shared basis
fresh rank-2 LoRA factors fitted from the same 32 support examples
metrics: actual full serialized bytes including frozen bases and new-skill state

storage.authority: actual compressed NPZ inference payload bytes
paid_objects: new skill code or LoRA factors

success_gate: new skill nRMSE <=0.02, complete deployed bytes at least 25% lower than fresh LoRA, and lower adaptation operations without worse quality than native shared-basis code.
failure_gate: FAIL if native shared-basis code exactly matches Mirror or Mirror does not beat fresh LoRA on full bytes/quality/adaptation work.
boundaries: Synthetic linear action task only; no learned/physical robot skill claim.

Shared atoms and six base skill codes are generated and frozen before the new-skill support/test samples; this is a controlled synthetic addressability screen, not learned basis evidence. New-skill coefficient is inferred only from 32 support examples.
No fresh seeds after dev control alias or gate miss.
